lines.zh: 先做一个思想实验：我说，我养了一只……
lines.en: Let's start with a thought experiment. I say: I keep a pet...

lines.zh: 你脑子里大概已经跳出了「猫」或者「狗」。
lines.en: Your mind has probably already jumped to "cat" or "dog".

lines.zh: 几乎不可能是「微波炉」。
lines.en: It is almost certainly not "microwave."

lines.zh: 为什么？因为你读过很多中文，知道这里常出现哪些词。
lines.en: Why? Because you have read a lot of Chinese, and you know which words tend to appear here.

lines.zh: 你对语言的把握，至少有一部分，就表现为对下一个词的预期。
lines.en: At least part of your grasp of language shows up as an expectation about the next word.

lines.zh: 这一章，我们把这种预期，变成一个可以计算的东西。
lines.en: In this chapter, we turn that expectation into something computable.

scenes.zh: 一台只做一件事的机器

lines.zh: 假设模型的词表里只有四个词：猫、狗、鱼、车。
lines.en: Suppose the model's vocabulary has only four words: cat, dog, fish, car.

lines.zh: 对于刚才那句话，模型给出的不是答案，而是一组概率。
lines.en: For that sentence, the model does not give an answer. It gives a set of probabilities.

lines.zh: 四个数字加起来等于一，因为它们是一个概率分布。
lines.en: The four numbers add up to one, because they form a probability distribution.

lines.zh: 这就是语言模型的全部秘密：输入一段文本，输出词表上的一个分布。
lines.en: That is the whole secret of a language model: text in, a distribution over the vocabulary out.

lines.zh: 注意两个细节，它们后面会变得非常重要。
lines.en: Two details matter, and both will become important later.

lines.zh: 第一，输出是分布，不是一个词。选哪个词，是后面的采样策略决定的。
lines.en: First, the output is a distribution, not a word. The choice is made by a sampling strategy, covered later.

lines.zh: 这也解释了，为什么同一个问题问两次，答案可能不一样。
lines.en: That also explains why the same question asked twice can get different answers.

lines.zh: 第二，上文可以任意长。而这个承诺，正是 Transformer 要解决的问题。
lines.en: Second, the context can be arbitrarily long. That promise is exactly what the Transformer was built to keep.

lines.zh: 模型一次只预测一个词。那整句话的概率怎么算？
lines.en: The model predicts one word at a time. So how do we get the probability of a whole sentence?

lines.zh: 用概率论的链式法则，也就是高中学过的乘法公式，反复用。
lines.en: Use the chain rule of probability: the multiplication rule from high school, applied again and again.

lines.zh: 「我养了一只猫」的概率，等于每个词在它前面所有词条件下的概率，连乘起来。
lines.en: The probability of "I keep a cat" is each word's probability given everything before it, multiplied together.

lines.zh: 写成公式：从第一个词到第 T 个词，每一步条件概率的乘积。
lines.en: In symbols: the product of the conditional probability at every step, from the first word to word T.

lines.zh: 这种用自己前面的输出，当作下一步输入的生成方式，叫自回归。
lines.en: Generating by feeding your own output back in as the next input is called autoregression.

lines.zh: 语言模型就像一座桥，每次只往前挪一步。
lines.en: A language model is like a bridge you cross one step at a time.

lines.zh: 整句话的概率，就是每一步概率的连乘。
lines.en: The probability of the sentence is the product of the probability of each step.

lines.zh: 但很多个小于一的数相乘，会迅速变成零，这叫下溢。
lines.en: But multiplying many numbers below one quickly collapses to zero. That is underflow.

lines.zh: 所以实际计算时取对数，把连乘变成连加。
lines.en: So in practice we take logarithms, turning the product into a sum.

lines.zh: 对数在这里不是装饰。下一节你会看到，它恰好对应信息量。
lines.en: The logarithm is not decoration. Next, you will see that it measures information.

lines.zh: 那么，这些概率是怎么来的？历史上先后有两代做法。
lines.en: So where do these probabilities come from? History offers two generations of answers.

lines.zh: 第一代是数数，叫 n-gram 模型。
lines.en: The first generation simply counted. These are n-gram models.

lines.zh: 想知道「我养了一只」后面跟「猫」的概率，就去数这个组合在文本库里出现了多少次。
lines.en: To estimate the probability of "cat" after "I keep a", count how often that combination appears in a corpus.

lines.zh: 为了不让历史太长、一次都数不到，通常只回看最近 n 减一个词。
lines.en: To avoid histories too long to ever be seen, it looks back only n minus one words.

lines.zh: 它有两个致命伤。
lines.en: It has two fatal weaknesses.

lines.zh: 第一是稀疏：语言组合是无穷的，没见过的组合，概率就是零。
lines.en: First, sparsity: word combinations are endless, and an unseen combination gets probability zero.

lines.zh: 第二是不共享：在它眼里，「猫」和「狗」是两个毫不相干的计数。
lines.en: Second, no sharing: to an n-gram model, "cat" and "dog" are two unrelated counts.

lines.zh: 2003 年，Bengio 等人换了个方向：给每个词一个向量。
lines.en: In 2003, Bengio and colleagues changed direction: give every word a vector.

lines.zh: 相似的词，向量也相似；再用神经网络，算出下一个词的概率。
lines.en: Similar words get similar vectors, and a neural network turns them into next-word probabilities.

lines.zh: 一句话：n-gram 在记忆组合，神经语言模型在学习关系。
lines.en: In one line: n-grams memorize combinations; neural language models learn relationships.

lines.zh: 见过「我养了一只猫」，它自然也会给「我养了一只狗」不低的概率。
lines.en: Having seen "I keep a cat", it naturally gives "I keep a dog" a decent probability too.

lines.zh: 而这张「词向量到神经网络」的图，就是十七年后 GPT 的骨架。
lines.en: And that diagram, vectors into a network, is the skeleton of GPT seventeen years later.

lines.zh: 模型给出一组概率。怎么判断它猜得好不好？
lines.en: The model outputs a distribution. How do we judge how well it guessed?

lines.zh: 先从「意外」说起。
lines.en: Start with surprise.

lines.zh: 明天下雨的概率是 0.99，真下雨了，你不意外。
lines.en: If rain tomorrow has probability 0.99, rain does not surprise you.

lines.zh: 概率是 0.01，真下雨了，你很意外。
lines.en: If the probability is 0.01, rain surprises you a lot.

lines.zh: 所以意外程度，应该是概率的减函数。
lines.en: So surprise should decrease as probability increases.

lines.zh: 而且两个独立事件同时发生，意外应该等于各自意外之和。
lines.en: And for two independent events, surprise should add up.

lines.zh: 满足这两条的，本质上只有一个函数：负 log p。
lines.en: Essentially one function satisfies both: minus log p.

lines.zh: 这叫信息量。概率为一，信息量为零；概率趋近于零，信息量趋于无穷。
lines.en: This is information content. Probability one gives zero; probability near zero gives near infinity.

lines.zh: 把每种结果的意外，按概率平均，就是熵。
lines.en: Average that surprise over outcomes, weighted by probability, and you get entropy.

lines.zh: 公平硬币的熵是一比特；永远正面的硬币，熵是零。
lines.en: A fair coin has one bit of entropy. A coin that always lands heads has zero.

lines.zh: 现在是关键的一步。
lines.en: Now comes the key step.

lines.zh: 真实世界有一个分布 p，模型给出一个分布 q。
lines.en: The world has a true distribution p. The model gives a distribution q.

lines.zh: 用 q 去编码来自 p 的事件，平均意外程度，就是交叉熵。
lines.en: Encoding events from p with q gives an average surprise: the cross-entropy.

lines.zh: 它等于 p 自己的熵，加上一个叫 KL 散度的东西。
lines.en: It equals the entropy of p, plus a term called the KL divergence.

lines.zh: KL 散度衡量两个分布的差异，永远非负。
lines.en: KL divergence measures the gap between two distributions, and is never negative.

lines.zh: 而 p 的熵是数据本身的性质，不随模型变。
lines.en: The entropy of p belongs to the data, and does not change with the model.

lines.zh: 所以最小化交叉熵，就是最小化 KL 散度，也就是让模型分布尽量接近真实分布。
lines.en: So minimizing cross-entropy means minimizing KL divergence: moving the model distribution toward the truth.

lines.zh: 几乎所有的语言模型，都用交叉熵当损失函数。
lines.en: Almost every language model uses cross-entropy as its loss.

lines.zh: 回到刚才的四词表。真实答案是猫，模型给了 0.60，交叉熵约等于 0.51 奈特。
lines.en: Back to the four-word vocabulary: answer cat, model says 0.60, cross-entropy is about 0.51 nats.

lines.zh: 如果真实答案是车，模型只给了 0.02，交叉熵约等于 3.91。
lines.en: If the answer is car and the model gives only 0.02, cross-entropy is about 3.91.

lines.zh: 猜错的代价，是猜对的七点七倍。
lines.en: Being wrong here costs 7.7 times as much as being right.

lines.zh: 交叉熵对「自信地猜错」，惩罚极重。
lines.en: Cross-entropy punishes confident mistakes very heavily.

lines.zh: 把奈特翻译成人话：取 e 的指数，得到困惑度。
lines.en: To translate nats into plain language, exponentiate: that gives perplexity.

lines.zh: 1.67 的困惑度，意思是平均在不到两个词之间犹豫。
lines.en: A perplexity of 1.67 means the model hesitates between fewer than two words on average.

lines.zh: 如果对五万个词完全均匀地乱猜，困惑度正好是五万。
lines.en: Guessing uniformly among fifty thousand words gives a perplexity of exactly fifty thousand.

lines.zh: 把交叉熵画成曲线：横轴是模型给正确答案的概率 q，纵轴是 −log q。
lines.en: Plot cross-entropy: the x-axis is the probability q the model gives the correct answer; the y-axis is −log q.

lines.zh: q 越接近零，曲线越陡；KL 就是交叉熵高出熵的那一段。
lines.en: As q approaches zero, the curve gets steeper; KL is the part of cross-entropy above entropy.

lines.zh: 交叉熵等于熵加 KL。训练要压掉的，就是 KL 这一段。
lines.en: Cross-entropy equals entropy plus KL. Training squeezes down that KL part.

lines.zh: 把上面串起来，训练目标就很自然了。
lines.en: Put it all together, and the training objective writes itself.

lines.zh: 调整参数，让真实的下一个词，在模型分布下的平均负对数概率最小。
lines.en: Tune the parameters so the true next word has the lowest average negative log probability.

lines.zh: 这个式子还有第二个身份：最大似然估计。
lines.en: This expression has a second identity: maximum likelihood estimation.

lines.zh: 因为最小化负对数似然，等价于最大化似然。
lines.en: Minimizing negative log-likelihood is the same as maximizing likelihood.

lines.zh: 也就是，让模型认为训练语料尽可能可能发生。
lines.en: In other words, make the training corpus as likely as possible under the model.

lines.zh: 从信息论看，这叫最小化交叉熵；从统计学看，这叫最大似然。
lines.en: Information theory calls it minimizing cross-entropy; statistics calls it maximum likelihood.

lines.zh: 同一件事的两种语言，会贯穿整门课。
lines.en: Two languages for one thing, and this pattern runs through the whole course.

lines.zh: 至于具体怎么调参数，是下一章的主题。
lines.en: How to actually tune those parameters is the next chapter.

lines.zh: 模型最后吐出的，其实不是概率，而是一组任意实数，叫 logit。
lines.en: What the model finally emits is not a probability but a set of arbitrary real numbers, called logits.

lines.zh: 把它变成概率，用 softmax。
lines.en: Turn them into probabilities with softmax.

lines.zh: 每个 logit 先取指数，再除以所有指数之和。
lines.en: Exponentiate each logit, then divide by the sum of all exponentials.

lines.zh: 分母里多了一个温度参数，控制分布的锋利程度。
lines.en: The denominator includes a temperature parameter that controls how sharp the distribution is.

lines.zh: 温度趋近于零，几乎全给最大的 logit，输出确定。
lines.en: As temperature approaches zero, almost all mass goes to the largest logit, and output becomes deterministic.

lines.zh: 温度等于一，是原始分布；大于一，分布变平，冷门词也有机会。
lines.en: At one you get the original distribution. Above one it flattens, giving rare words a chance.

lines.zh: 这跟统计力学里的玻尔兹曼分布完全同构：logit 对应负能量，温度对应温度。
lines.en: This is exactly the Boltzmann distribution: logits are negative energy, temperature is temperature.

lines.zh: 只看两个候选词：横轴是 logit 差，纵轴是较高那个的概率。
lines.en: Take just two candidates: the x-axis is the logit difference, the y-axis is the probability of the higher one.

lines.zh: 温度越小，曲线越像台阶；温度越大，曲线越平缓。
lines.en: The lower the temperature, the more the curve looks like a step; the higher it is, the flatter the curve.

lines.zh: 有了分布，还要决定怎么选词，这叫解码。
lines.en: With a distribution in hand, we still choose a word. That step is called decoding.

lines.zh: 贪心，永远选概率最大的，确定但容易重复。
lines.en: Greedy decoding always takes the top word: deterministic, but prone to repetition.

lines.zh: 纯采样，按概率抽，多样但可能离谱。
lines.en: Pure sampling draws by probability: diverse, but sometimes wild.

lines.zh: top-k 只在最高的 k 个里抽；top-p 只在累积概率达到 p 的最小集合里抽。
lines.en: Top-k samples from the k most likely words; top-p from the smallest set whose mass reaches p.

lines.zh: 这些都是推理时的旋钮，不改模型本身。
lines.en: All of these are knobs at inference time. They do not change the model itself.

lines.zh: 最后，看看这个目标的天花板和地板。
lines.en: Finally, look at the floor and the ceiling of this objective.

lines.zh: 地板是：只会预测下一个词的模型，在 2003 年只能做很有限的事。
lines.en: The floor: in 2003, a model that only predicts the next word could do very little.

lines.zh: 它需要大量数据、大量算力，还需要一个能记住长上文的架构。
lines.en: It needed lots of data, lots of compute, and an architecture that could remember a long context.

lines.zh: 天花板是一个值得反复思考的问题。
lines.en: The ceiling is a question worth returning to.

lines.zh: 要准确预测「这道积分等于」，模型必须真的会算积分吗？
lines.en: To predict "this integral equals", must the model actually know how to integrate?

lines.zh: 还是只要记住，这类题后面常跟哪个数字就够了？
lines.en: Or is it enough to remember which numbers tend to follow such problems?

lines.zh: 答案是：在训练数据覆盖的范围内，记忆就够了；一旦超出，就必须学会规则。
lines.en: The answer: inside the training distribution, memory suffices. Outside it, the model must learn rules.

lines.zh: 而学会规则这件事，会在规模变大时自发发生。
lines.en: And learning rules happens spontaneously as scale grows.

lines.zh: 这就是为什么，一个看似平庸的目标，最终逼出了推理。
lines.en: That is why such a plain objective eventually forced reasoning into existence.

lines.zh: 但也别过度浪漫化。它优化的是文本上的条件概率，不是世界的真相。
lines.en: But do not romanticize it. It optimizes conditional probability over text, not the truth of the world.

lines.zh: 这两者的缝隙，就是幻觉的来源。
lines.en: The gap between the two is where hallucinations come from.

lines.zh: 这一章，我们有了目标函数。
lines.en: This chapter gave us an objective function.

lines.zh: 但还没有回答：参数怎么自动变好？
lines.en: But we have not answered how parameters improve by themselves.

lines.zh: 下一章讲梯度下降与反向传播。
lines.en: The next chapter covers gradient descent and backpropagation.

lines.zh: 全课程第一个陡坡，也是整个深度学习的发动机。
lines.en: The first steep climb of the course, and the engine of all deep learning.

lines.zh: 第二章，梯度与反向传播。我们下期见。
lines.en: Chapter two: gradients and backpropagation. See you next time.
